subject: Best practices when developing shiny app with large UI portion?

messages.author: a1bf76ab9a5a2d4b
messages.subject: Best practices when developing shiny app with large UI portion?
parts:
I'm wondering if anyone has any thoughts or if there are any standards on how to deal with apps with a lot of UI.

I'm building a fairly complex app and having everything in one ui.R file seems very messy.  My app has a few different tabs, so I was thinking of having each tabPanel in a separate file and have a function in each file that returns the tags for one tab. Thoughts?


It would be something like this:

ui.R
library(shiny)

source("tab-dataset.R")
source("tab-analyze.R")
source("tab-plot.R")

shinyUI(navbarPage(
  getTabDataset(),
  getTabAnalyze(),
  getTabPlot()
))


tab-dataset.R
getTabDataset <- function() {
  tabPanel(
    ...
  )
}

And similarly for the other tabs

messages.author: 8e72bac5f7bfb16e
messages.subject: Re: Best practices when developing shiny app with large UI portion?
parts:
Thọ Duy Nguyễn's reference to the 'build your entire interface in HTML' is very interesting.

However, I think Dean's suggestion for separating pieces of the UI into separate files is very good.  My only suggestion
would be to add a file naming convention, like precede all UI related files with "ui-" or some such, e.g. "ui-tab-dataset.R",
so then you see all the ui files at a glance when you look at a directory listing.

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Best practices when developing shiny app with large UI portion?
parts:
You could just do this:

library(shiny)

shinyUI(navbarPage(
  source("tab-dataset.R", local = TRUE)$value,
  source("tab-analyze.R", local = TRUE)$value,
  source("tab-plot.R", local = TRUE)$value
))

And the tab-*.R files would just contain tabPanel(...) itself, not a function to wrap it.
